sections.title: Music and the ideas it carries

exchanges.question: What made music the way to carry your systems and ideas, and what do you want someone to feel or understand when they hear a song before they know anything about your projects?
exchanges.answer: Music is the ultimate compression algorithm for humans with a proven history of passing knowledge across tens of thousands of years and unknown generations.

exchanges.question: Which of your songs best demonstrates that compression, and what knowledge or pattern do you want someone to carry away from it?
exchanges.answer: None stand out above the pack because they were all invented from the desire to inspire people and transfer complex awareness and deeper meaning through fun at a level that will be enjoyable to people across experience levels. But in the sense of civic participation it's got to be both The Purple Mat that Could, and We Go Beyond.

exchanges.question: In “We Go Beyond”, you write, “We don’t throw the brick, we fill every form.” Where did that approach to changing things come from in your own life?
exchanges.answer:
Lol, so you picked the line that is in both songs with very little variation.

[Pause] I mixed up the songs. I meant Don’t Throw a Brick, not The Purple Mat that Could. Lol.

Well it stems from my journey of being fed up with the status quo and feeling like the system did not represent the interests of the people like the stories of my elders who were in the labour and union movement.

In 2012/13 I took time off over the summer to go through my filing cabinet and make note of every fine print statute that was referenced, read them cover to cover and followed the references to understand the system as best I could.

Following that I wanted to opt out of Australia and representative democracy. I found the Canadian freeman movement, I think they call it now in Australia the sovereign citizens and tried that for a couple of years as a frustrated bloke testing the boundaries of the container holding me. I found that it was a thorough container and no matter what words were used or codes invoked, the enforcers did not accept the authority of a human that did not have a standing of granted authority from the system.

So I then decided that the only way out was through. That eventually turned into my plans for gamify democracy, then 10 years later that turned into P4A and ethical overcompliance, music and art with sophisticated systems that use the rules of the bounding box to force the environment and its masters to change.

exchanges.question: When you say “the only way out was through”, what is one practical example of using the system’s own rules to get a fairer outcome, either something you’ve done or something you want to make possible?
exchanges.answer:
Self reflection is the real crux of it. If you're in a box with rules and you become aware of the rules, that's like realising the box is a mirror. Then you have to examine yourself according to the reflection, and then you realise you can invent another mirror by using the rules and exposing the rules. So you hold up a mirror to a mirror that creates a paradox and you open infinity.

If I can face my demons and then confidently hold up a mirror to the system and its office holders, the door opens and then the deeper meaning of where the door goes to becomes the focus.

exchanges.question: What has facing your own demons changed about the way you listen to someone who disagrees with you?
exchanges.answer: Lol, who's the audience? Basically I have more patience. I see myself and the light in everything and everyone. There's mirrors everywhere with abstractions and distortions created from their evolutionary perspective. We are all light, atoms, electricity and magnetism tied together with perspective or soul.

exchanges.question: Given that your outlook and projects reach well beyond local government, what draws you to the mayor’s role specifically?
exchanges.answer:
The mayoral role is just a small piece in the macro puzzle. If it was a full term I would not consider it. I have a bigger aim.

However, seeing as I have already submitted my request for a pilot zone of the Community Hour or C-hour to the federal inquiry into local government funding and fiscal responsibility in January, and the role came up, I just figured it was a reasonable diversion.

I had also been giving my research and development to local councillors and the acting mayor and the state and federal reps of Straddie but I didn't feel like the emails and meetings were landing. I felt they just brushed me off and continued on their way. So I figured I'd make myself impossible to ignore.

exchanges.question: What does that bigger aim look like to you, and where does Redlands sit within it?
exchanges.answer:
GAJRA Earth, a global association for joyful responsible abundance on Earth and a Fair Go in the Age of Superintelligence. Look we all know that China and USA are going hell for leather towards superintelligence supremacy. It's probably more the USA trying to maintain dominance and China being a challenging contender but it doesn't matter really who is of which intent, when the media convinces everyone in day to day life that this is the most important thing since fire, or electricity or the atom bomb and it could wipe out humanity, and if someone wins AI they rule the world.

So lots of people and companies are aiming for the pinnacle without any real plan on what they would do if they win, or how to prevent it going out of control.

I took a position in my UNGA81 open document to the question of the UNGA about restoring trust in multilateralism to imagine that every person has a red button that will end the game of life. In symbology let’s call it the nuclear launch codes, superintelligence or SI.

While everyone else is talking about safeguards and stopping the button from getting into the hands of people at all, I simply asked "What would make life so enjoyable and interesting that even if everyone had that button, no one would ever want to press it?"

exchanges.question: How do you get from that question to the practical design of GAJRA Earth?
exchanges.answer:
I worked out that compassionate joyful responsible abundance were ideal concepts to aspire to for a fulfilling life that I had not experienced in regularity only glimpses. I had intuition that it was the direction everyone is attracted to if they forgive themselves enough to feel like they deserve fulfilment, and then when I was looking for acronyms I found that a gajra is a flower garland in India and Asia and 1+1 I dropped the compassionate and made it GAJRA Earth.

I have lots of weird and wonderful and terrible and funny and stupid acronyms. This one stuck.

exchanges.question: Can you tell me about one of those glimpses of fulfilment, and what made it feel different?
exchanges.answer: Simple moments really when people actually seem to see through the masks we wear every day and just resonate with love, trust, understanding and belief.

exchanges.question: What’s one everyday change you’d want people in Redlands to experience through this work?
exchanges.answer: To share time together with more open hearts and minds, remembering we're all in this together.

exchanges.question: What would taking part in a C-hour look like for someone in Redlands who’s never heard of it?
exchanges.answer:
It's not something that will happen overnight. It's a parallel ledger to the monetary economy that would need us to learn some new tools and ways of thinking but it's basically about building a reciprocity economy based on time and radical equality instead of market economics of assets and inequality due to skill or authority.

Either economy on their own won't really work effectively for the benefit of the majority but I believe that braided together they can work much better than the world we know today.

exchanges.question: What does “radical equality” mean in practice when people contribute different skills, resources or levels of ability?
exchanges.answer:
Everyone’s one hour is worth exactly one C-hour.

Any benefit is decided by the community and/or the individuals. It's like if you play a computer game and there's certain things you need money for but there's other quests that are integral to the most interesting paths that you cannot buy, you have to contribute time and earn social favours.

The C-hour is a ledger for friends, groups and the wider society while managing the mainstream and bigger projects with commerce. It repairs the social fabric.

exchanges.question: What’s something you’d like people to know about you that doesn’t come through in the websites?
Yes, you as a person. What would someone discover about you spending an afternoon together that they wouldn’t get from reading your websites?
exchanges.answer:
Um, I'm a complicated weirdo who’s also simple and normal. A paradox of interesting experiences and bigger than average hopes and dreams. I'm a hermit, and an outlandish fool sometimes. I explore biases and test boundaries but respect the others I'm in the game with.

2027 will be my 44th orbit of the sun and I hope it's enjoyable, responsible and I meet a lot of new interesting people, maybe attract and share a bit of love along the way.

exchanges.question: Can you tell me about a time your “outlandish fool” side led to an encounter or experience you’re glad you had?
exchanges.answer: Travelling alone overseas. Saying yes to opportunities that I knew little about, saying no to people who tell me something I want to aim for is impossible.
